chunks: That was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a newborn who is born on the night of al-Fiṭr, and a Jew or a Christian who accepts Islam on the night of al-Fiṭr,
He عليه السلام said: “There is no fiṭrah upon them. The fiṭrah is only upon one who has reached the month.”

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ الشَّهْرَ: having reached or lived through the month of Ramadan
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian, mentioned as one who may newly enter Islam
key_terms.الْمَوْلُودِ: the newborn child being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew, mentioned as one who may newly enter Islam
key_terms.فِطْرَةٌ: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْفِطْرِ: the night of Eid al-Fitr, the time relevant to the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat al-Fitr obligatory for a baby born or a person who accepts Islam on the night of Eid al-Fitr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on Zakat al-Fitr for those who only enter the state of obligation at the very end of Ramadan, such as a child born on the night of Eid al-Fitr or a non-Muslim who embraces Islam that night. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that Zakat al-Fitr is only due from one who had already lived through and reached the month.
